name: Lichen Green
lede: Lichen green is a very pale, cool green, named for the whitish green of lichen.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines *lichen-green* as the whitish green of the lichen plant [1]. The swatch is a very pale green, matching the ISCC-NBS name very pale green [2]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas carries the name on an aged plate, approximate, and the Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 dates it to 1898 [2]. It is a quiet cousin of [[light-green]], [[lettuce-green]] and [[moss-green]], in the family of [[green]] [2].

The books add no history of the name, so none is claimed [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 99, 0.42 per cent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1800s, at 1.4 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it is usually a light, as in 68 per cent of 80 paintings [3]. Alfred Sisley uses it in 4 of the 50 works we hold, 5.5 times the baseline [3]. In Google Books the word peaks in the 1920s [4].
